$comment: Review-lanes manifest (ADR-0011 decision A, #2869/#2870). A lane is a named row
here and nowhere else: this file is the only place an endpoint, a
credential binding, an egress host, a default model or a cost basis for the
dogfood AI review may be defined. No workflow expression derives any of
them from the vars context. Which row a run uses is selected by the
repository variable LINTRO_AI_PROVIDER, read only by the secret-free lane
job: it must name a row here, unset means chain[0], and anything else
fails closed before a secret is exposed. LINTRO_AI_MODEL, read the same
way, overrides the selected row's default model; unset means the row's.
chain is the default lane followed by the fallback order of decision D.
scripts/ci/resolve_review_lanes.py validates this file and the two
variables and fails closed, naming the declared lanes.
credential_secret names the organisation or repository secret the workflow forwards by one
literal secrets.<NAME> expression; credential_env names the environment
VARIABLE the CLI reads it from (for z.ai and Kimi, the secret fills
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN). A file-form credential is materialised by the
wrapper at credential_file from credential_source_env, the variable the
secret is injected into, for the length of one attempt. Nothing in this
file is a secret.
base_url_env is the provider override the CLI reads; null means the CLI
reads none, and the lane endpoint must then be the CLI's built-in one.
model is the row's default, used when LINTRO_AI_MODEL is unset; every row
names one, so no run falls through to a CLI's own default. There is no
allowed-model list: the operator chooses the model, the sticky reports
what answered.
first_party must agree with the endpoint: true only on the provider's own
host (anthropic api.anthropic.com, openai api.openai.com, cursor
api2.cursor.sh); a non-first-party row carries cost_basis unknown.
priced_models lists the models lintro carries a non-zero list-price table
for (tests/scripts/ci/test_resolve_review_lanes.py pins it to the
registry); a row whose default model is not in it must declare
shadow_price_model, as must every non-first-party row (decision B).
Owner decision 2026-10-16: zai and kimi are declared gateway rows; either
becomes active by setting LINTRO_AI_PROVIDER to its id.
anthropic's shadow_price_model is a stand-in until lintro carries Claude 5.5 list tables; on list_price_shadow the envelope's own figure is used and the stand-in prices nothing.
smoke_row names the row of scripts/ci/ai_provider_smoke/providers.json whose
weekly call stands for this lane (#2873), and smoke_covers says how much of
the lane that call proves. 'route': the row sends the lane's own secret down
the lane's own path, so a dead token and a dead path both go red (zai, kimi).
'host': the lane's credential is a subscription session the raw API cannot
take, so the row sends the provider's metered key to the same host
the CLI calls; it proves the host answers, not that the session is alive
(anthropic: the claude CLI calls api.anthropic.com/v1/messages). 'provider':
the session's own route is one no API smoke can reach, so the row proves
only that the provider's API answers (openai: the Codex session calls the
ChatGPT backend, chatgpt.com in the lane's egress, while openai-api calls
api.openai.com). An expired session is reported by the dogfood's own
auth_failed verdict on the next review, never by the smoke. A lane no smoke
can reach at all (cursor exposes no API protocol lintro implements) carries
smoke_row null and smoke_gap saying why.
tests/scripts/ci/test_smoke_rows_match_lanes.py holds the two files to this.

cursor.smoke_gap: cursor exposes no API protocol lintro implements; the CLI is the only transport
